doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Honeymoon alone in Buffalo and the jam session after the wedding
summary: Marty finished two weeks with the band after marrying, then went to a 4 a.m. jam at the Capitol Hotel.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well your career started when the big bands were pretty healthy.
And you obviously did marry your wife.
Well it’s stood the test of time anyway.

Oh boy I’m telling you. And then we went back to my mother’s house after we got married, she lived a block away, and we had a sandwich and a glass of milk and my wife walked me to the subway, and I went back to Pennsylvania, and I finished two weeks with the band, and I did my honeymoon alone in Buffalo. I said, “man, nobody’s had a honeymoon like this.” I spent my honeymoon alone man.

It was cold. I can’t believe how cold it gets in Buffalo. And anyway, that’s what happened. So listen to this, now here’s another funny story. I get back to New York and now we’re married, so we check into the Forrest Hotel, and the band that I was with has some time off, so we get married and we checked into the Forrest Hotel on 48th Street in New York, and about three o’clock in the morning the phone rings. Four o’clock in the morning. And I can’t even find the phone, it’s like on the floor or something. I said, “hello?” “Who’s this?” “Marty, this is Shelly Manne.” I says, “what’s happening, Shelly?” He says, “we’re having a jam session at the Capitol Hotel in the ballroom.” I says, “I’ll be right there.” So I hung up the phone, and my wife says, “where you going?” I says, “Shelly said they’re having a session.” So she says, “you’re not going without me.” So we got our clothes on, we went over there, and about 30 years later I’m doing a club date, a Jewish wedding someplace, and the drummer was a club date leader. He says, “Marty, do you know when you got married you went to a jam session at the Capitol Hotel.” I said, “how’d you know that?” He says, “I was playing drums.” And he says, “you know what? I looked over and your wife was sitting in the corner by you on the piano, falling asleep.” He says, “how dare you?” And my wife says, “yeah, if I knew he was going to do that, that would have been it, that would have been it.”
You know I think some script writer must have known about that because that’s the scene in the Glenn Miller story in the movie.
He gets married, he goes back to the hotel and all the guys show up at this thing and they go down and they hear Louis Armstrong.
